subject: Request: Exception for MFN + benchmark clause — Calyx Systems deal
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-22T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Calyx pilot — MFN + benchmark ask (need escalation)

Hi Chloe / Laura —

Following up from today's commercial call with Calyx (Nina, Marcus + legal on the thread). They asked for two items that are high risk for us but critical to close the $1.9M pilot:

- MFN on pricing vs any direct or channel offers for 18 months (they want a price-match guarantee across the healthcare vertical)
- A benchmark clause tying renewal pricing to an adoption metric (if monthly active devices > X then price reduces by Y)

They are also asking for a 30% up-front discount and a 6-month exclusive pilot window in North America for the "MedCare" product line. In exchange they are committing to a one-year SOW for volume and will introduce us to a strategic health system if pilot metrics are met.

Why I’m escalating: Deal desk flagged MFN + benchmark as high commercial risk (price erosion + administrative burden). Legal indicated MFN as written would be overly broad; finance needs to model unit economics under the discount + potential benchmark-triggered reduction.

Attachments: Calyx_SOW_v3.pdf (current SOW), Calyx_RFI_responses.pdf (compliance items). I also attached the counter MFN draft they sent (redwood-MFN-draft-annotated.docx) — see page 2-3 for their proposed language.

Ask: I recommend an exec exception if we can 1) narrow MFN scope (healthcare product line only), 2) limit MFN duration to 12 months, 3) define benchmark precisely and cap its downside (max additional discount 8%), and 4) keep exclusivity time-boxed to the pilot (90 days) with explicit termination if minimum usage floors not met.

Could Legal + Finance + RevOps review and confirm whether this conservative set of concessions would be acceptable to approve? If so, I’d like an executive sign-off today/tomorrow to keep momentum. Calyx is pushing deadline end of week.

Thanks —
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, chloe_martin <chloe@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Calyx pilot — MFN + benchmark ask (need escalation)

Ben / Chloe —

Thanks for the context. High-level Deal Desk read:

- MFN: Material risk. If we grant a broad MFN we lock price parity across future channel deals and could be forced to retroactively drop prices. Need a narrow definition (product/region/customer list).
- Benchmark pricing: Operationally complex. What triggers the benchmark (MAUs, sessions, throughput)? Who verifies? Need audit clause and a cap on downside.
- Exclusivity: Acceptable if strictly limited (pilot product only, NA only, 90-day max) and tied to clear KPIs.

Immediate asks for approval workflow:
1) Finance: model P&L under 30% discount + potential 8% benchmark reduction at three adoption tiers (low/med/high). Markus, can you run a quick sensitivity with expected pilot run-rate?
2) Legal: produce redline with narrow MFN language + enforcement/audit language. Rishi, can you add a sunset and carveouts (marketplace, channel resellers)?
3) RevOps: confirm whether we can operationalize the benchmark verification and reporting cadence. Aditya, quick note on telemetry/reporting overhead?

If everyone agrees on the mitigations above, I will prepare an executive summary for sign-off. We should also consider a conditional approval: allow the concession for this pilot only if Calyx signs SOW and accepts the reporting/audit terms.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Deal Desk Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, chloe_martin <chloe@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-23T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Calyx pilot — MFN + benchmark ask (legal redline attached)

Laura / Ben / Chloe —

Attached is an annotated redline (redwood-MFN-draft-annotated.docx) with recommended guardrails. Key legal mitigations:

1) MFN scope: Limit to the "MedCare" product family and to direct offers to Calyx (no channel or marketplace triggers).
2) Duration: Reduce MFN term to 12 months from execution.
3) Benchmark definition: Use a single objective metric (monthly active integrations) with an independent reporting cadence (monthly self-report + quarterly audit right).
4) Cap: Limit benchmark-triggered discount to 8% cumulative across the 12 months.
5) Enforcement: Require notice + cure period; prohibit retroactive pricing adjustments beyond 90 days.
6) Confidentiality and non-solicit: tighten language to prevent overly broad exclusivity.

I also recommend: require a minimum revenue floor (e.g., $400k ARR run-rate equivalent) or we reserve right to terminate exclusivity. If Calyx refuses these guardrails, we should not grant broad MFN or any open-ended benchmark that reduces price below our floor.

If Deal Desk and Finance can confirm economics, Legal can approve this redline for exec sign-off.

Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-24T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Exec approval request: conditional exception for Calyx (summary + recommended concessions)

Team —

Summary: Calyx Systems is ready to sign a $1.9M pilot SOW but requires MFN (18 months) + a benchmark-linked renewal discount and short exclusivity. Deal Desk + Legal have produced conservative guardrails (MFN limited to product family, 12-month sunset, benchmark cap at 8%, minimum revenue floor, audit rights). Finance still needs to confirm P&L but initial modeling suggests the deal remains profitable under the proposed constraints if adoption meets the expected mid-tier.

My recommended conditional approval (seeks executive sign-off):
1) Approve MFN limited to: MedCare product family, North America, 12 months.
2) Approve benchmark clause only if: metric = monthly active integrations, verification = monthly self-report + quarterly audit, cap = 8% total discount, and no retroactive price changes beyond 90 days.
3) Approve pilot exclusivity for 90 days only, conditional on meeting a 3-month adoption threshold; exclusivity terminates automatically if threshold not met.
4) Approve a one-time 30% up-front discount provided Calyx signs the SOW and DocuSign link is executed within 48 hours of approval.

Risks and mitigation: the MFN is the largest risk for future price erosion; the product-family/region carveouts + 12-month sunset mitigate runway risk. Finance (Markus) — please confirm in this thread with a short Yes/No on whether you can accept the modeled downside (I will include the numbers if needed). Aditya — confirm RevOps can implement monthly reporting and the quarterly audit workflow before we sign.

If we get Yes from Finance + RevOps + Legal's redline accepted, I propose the following sign-off flow: CFO (Markus) => CRO (CC'd on separate thread) for final executive approval. I am happy to draft the one-page exec memo.

Please reply with explicit "Approve conditional exception" or "Decline". Timing is tight — vendor deadline is EOW.

Thanks,
Chloe

--
Chloe Martin
Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
